question: where a Flash-Next prefill spends its time, and what the ideas published by halogen, pwilkin and halo-box would buy on this file
setup: production profile (ctx 262144, batch = ubatch 8192, MTP draft ubatch 2048, QSA on), model Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-IQ4_XS, launched by tools/decode_lab.py --model <id>; node timing needs HIP graphs off and brackets every dispatch with events, graph timing synchronises after every graph, so both arms read ~2-4% slower than production (853.8 t/s here against 886 measured before at 85K)

real_text_prefill.prompt: tmp/realtext.txt: llama.cpp docs, READMEs and src/llama-*.cpp, 340000 chars = 95582 tokens
real_text_prefill.per_8192_batch: target GPU 7.7 -> 9.4 s as depth grows; set_inputs 0.20-0.70 s with the GPU idle (most likely the PLE row gather - hashed n-gram rows per token read from the 28.8 GB table on disk; not timed on its own; the prefetch only sees the batch it is in, and batch = ubatch); graph build + alloc 0.04-0.15 s; then the MTP draft prefills the same 8192 tokens in four 2048-token ubatches, 0.29-0.45 s, 65 ms of it prep on the CPU

gpu_per_op.note: random-word prompt (tools/decode_lab.py), 78939 tokens after a 2329-token prefix; kinds aggregated by op and shape, the time of a fused group charged to its first node

first_ubatch_depth_2.3K.graph: 17487 nodes, 4897 dispatches, 7592 ms of GPU time

last_ubatch_depth_73K.graph: 17511 nodes, 4909 dispatches, 9151 ms of GPU time

reading.experts: routed gate/up (IQ3_S through MMB_GLU) + down: ~2.1 s of 7.6, 17-21 TFLOPS - already the fused matrix-core path
reading.hyper-connections: the 4-stream residual (hc_dim 10240, F32) is normed, projected down to 320 and up to 10240, sigmoid-gated, mixed and re-injected in each of 96 sublayers. The combine + next norm is already one fused, bandwidth-bound kernel (hc_combine_norm, charged to SCALE [4]: 6 ms a call). The rest is not: hc_up MUL_MAT [10240] (~4.7 ms) + SIGMOID [10240] (3.6 ms) + the mix, and hc_down MUL_MAT [320] (3.7 ms) + inject MUL_MAT [4] (3.7 ms, a 4-row output on a 128-row tile), ~1.5 s of the 7.6. The fused kernels for exactly these (hc_gate_mix: GEMM + sigmoid + mix; MMB_TALL: down and inject in one pass over the activations) exist in the base but require IQ4_NL weights; this file has Q8_0 HC weights, so LLAMA_HC_GATEMIX, LLAMA_HC_PACK_DI and LLAMA_MMB_TALL, all set by the manager, never fire (no HC_GATEMIX or MMB_TALL line in any log). Likewise the PLE conv fusion matches only an F16 conv weight and this file has F32, so LLAMA_PLE_CONV is inert too. Plausibly part of why the all-IQ4_NL file prefilled at 1020 t/s against 903 (dead-ends.md), which was put down to the expert type.
reading.depth: first to last ubatch +1.56 s: FLASH_ATTN_EXT (QSA3) 375 -> 589 ms, TOP_K 0 -> 247 ms, K/V packing 57 ms, and a general ~5% (clock) - sparse attention keeps depth cheap
reading.gdn: GATED_DELTA_NET 470-566 ms + its gated norm ~360 ms + SSM_CONV 122 ms: ~12%

ab.ubatch 16384: batch = ubatch 16384, same prompt, one run each: 853.8 -> 876.6 t/s (+2.7%); loads at ctx 262144. Smaller than the +6% gfx1151-engine reports for 8K -> 16K.
ab.ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=1: 853.8 -> 856.4 t/s (+0.3%, noise): the GEMMs that carry the time run on MMB, not rocBLAS (pwilkin measured +3.1% where his bf16 GEMMs did run on rocBLAS)
